question.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 3,\,\,1\le y\le 2\}.$
Find the moment of inertia of this plate about the line $x=1.$
question.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Next, the area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=2\cdot 1=2.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{M}{2}|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{M}{2}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{2}({\int }_{1}^{3}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot [\frac{1}{3}(x-1)^{3}]_{1}^{3}\cdot {[y]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{2}(\frac{1}{3}(3-1)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}(1-1)^{3})\cdot (2-1) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}(\frac{8}{3}-0)\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{4M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
